title: The Divinity of Our Lord Jesus Christ
author: Dn Yonnas
summary: A Scriptural study of the divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ: that the Son is true God, of one essence with the Father, eternally begotten and not created. It walks through the direct testimonies of Christ's Godhead, the divine attributes manifested in Him, and the witness of the Transfiguration, Resurrection, and Ascension, read through the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo faith.

sections.h2: Introduction: One Lord, True God of True God

sections.p: The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church confesses with the whole Church of the Apostles that our Lord Jesus Christ is true God, of one essence (homoousios) with the Father, begotten of the Father before all worlds, light of light, very God of very God, begotten and not made. This study gathers the witness of Holy Scripture to this truth so that the faithful might be grounded in it and able to defend it. Against Arius, who taught that there was a time when the Son was not and that He was a creature, the Church proclaims that the Word is co-eternal with the Father, uncreated, and without beginning.

The word Tewahedo itself means “made one” or “unity,” confessing the perfect union of the full divinity and full humanity in the one incarnate Person of the Word. Because He who became man is God by nature, everything that Scripture ascribes to God it also ascribes to Him. The arguments below proceed from this foundation.

sections.h2: A. Clear and Direct Verses That Name Christ as God

sections.p: Scripture does not leave the Godhead of Christ to inference alone; it states it plainly. The outline begins with four passages that name or directly imply that Jesus is God.

John 1:1 declares: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Three statements are made: the Word existed “in the beginning,” before all created things; the Word was “with God,” a distinct Person in relation to the Father; and the Word “was God,” sharing the very nature of God. The phrase “in the beginning” echoes Genesis 1:1, but where Genesis speaks of the start of creation, John speaks of the Word who already was when the beginning began. He is therefore not part of creation but its uncreated source.

John 1:14 continues: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.” The same Word who was God took flesh. The Tewahedo confession rests here: the eternal God did not change into flesh nor merely associate with a man, but the Word truly became flesh, uniting humanity to His Godhead in one Person. His glory beheld by the disciples is the glory of God Himself.

John 10:30 records the Lord's own words: “I and my Father are one.” This is a claim to oneness of essence, not merely of will or purpose, as the response of His hearers shows: they took up stones, charging that He, being a man, made Himself God (John 10:33). The Lord did not retract the claim. He is one with the Father in nature, distinct from Him in Person.

Acts 20:28 speaks of “the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.” The blood shed on the Cross is here called the blood of God. Since God in His divine nature has no blood, this verse witnesses to the union of natures in Christ: the One who shed His blood as man is God in Person. This is why the Church does not divide Christ into two sons but confesses one Christ, God incarnate.

sections.h2: B. God's Unlimited Characteristics That Existed in the Lord Jesus Christ

sections.p: A creature is bounded; only God possesses the infinite attributes of deity. The outline shows that the attributes proper to God alone were truly present and active in the Lord Jesus Christ, proving that He is God by nature and not by adoption or honor.

In John 8:58 the Lord says, “Before Abraham was, I am.” He does not say “before Abraham was, I was,” but uses the divine name “I AM” (Exodus 3:14), claiming eternal, timeless existence. Abraham came into being; the Son simply IS. The Jews understood this as a claim to deity and again took up stones (John 8:59).

In John 17:5 the Lord prays, “And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.” He possessed divine glory in the presence of the Father before the world existed. A creature cannot have shared glory with God before creation; only the eternal Son can. This confirms that He is begotten of the Father before all worlds, not created in time.

sections.h3: Authority over Creation and the Power to Create

sections.p: John 9 recounts the healing of the man born blind, whom the Lord healed by anointing his eyes with clay made from spittle and dust. In forming sight from clay, the Lord does the very work of the Creator who formed man from the dust of the ground (Genesis 2:7). The act reveals the Creator's hand at work in Christ; as John 1:3 teaches, “all things were made by him.” He does not borrow creative power; it is His own.

sections.h3: He Is the Giver of Life

sections.p: In John 11:43-44 the Lord cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come forth,” and the dead man, four days in the tomb, came out alive. To call the dead back to life by His own word is the prerogative of God, who alone is the fountain of life. The Lord raises Lazarus not by petition alone but by command, exercising the authority over life and death that belongs to the Creator.

In Matthew 14:25 the Lord walked upon the sea, and in Matthew 14:32 the wind ceased when He entered the boat. The sea and the winds, which obey no man, obey Him. In Matthew 17:27 He directs Peter to find the tribute coin in the mouth of a fish, showing His sovereign knowledge and command over the creatures of the deep. As Psalm 89:9 says of the Lord, “Thou rulest the raging of the sea”; this dominion is exercised by Christ as His own.

In Luke 4:41 the demons came out of many, crying, “Thou art Christ the Son of God,” and He rebuked them. In Mark 1:13 the angels ministered to Him in the wilderness. In Matthew 26:51-53 He tells Peter that He could pray to the Father and be given more than twelve legions of angels. The angels serve Him and the demons are subject to His rebuke, for He is their Lord and Maker, not a fellow creature among them.

Taken together these characteristics, eternity, creative power, the giving of life, mastery of nature, and lordship over the spiritual hosts, are attributes that belong to God alone. Their full presence in the Lord Jesus is decisive proof of His true and proper divinity.

sections.h2: C. The Transfiguration, the Resurrection, and the Ascension

sections.p: The closing witnesses of the outline are three great manifestations in which the hidden glory of the incarnate God was revealed to His disciples and to the world.

In Matthew 17:2 the Lord “was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.” On Mount Tabor the disciples beheld the uncreated glory of His Godhead shining through His flesh. This is the glory of which John 1:14 spoke, the glory of the only-begotten of the Father. The Transfiguration shows that the splendor of divinity dwelt in Him always, veiled in His humanity and disclosed at His will.

sections.h3: The Power Displayed at His Arrest

sections.p: In John 18:5-8, when the soldiers came to arrest Him and He answered, “I am he,” they went backward and fell to the ground. By the mere word of the divine “I AM” those who came against Him were cast down. He gave Himself up freely; He was not taken by force. This shows that His Passion was a voluntary self-offering of the God who came to save, not the defeat of a helpless man.

Acts 1:2-11 records that after His suffering He showed Himself alive by many infallible proofs, and then was taken up while the disciples watched, a cloud receiving Him out of their sight, with the promise that He shall so come again. He who rose by His own power and ascended to the right hand of the Father is God. The Resurrection vindicates His claim to be the life-giver, and the Ascension restores to His glorified humanity the throne of glory He had with the Father before the world was (John 17:5).

sections.h2: Conclusion: Glory Be to the Holy Trinity

sections.p: From the direct testimony of Scripture, from the unlimited divine attributes manifest in Him, and from the glory revealed in His Transfiguration, Resurrection, and Ascension, the conclusion is firm: our Lord Jesus Christ is true God. He is of one essence with the Father, begotten of Him before all worlds, uncreated and eternal. Against every Arian denial, the Church confesses Him as very God of very God.

Yet this divine Word truly became flesh for our salvation, uniting full humanity to His full Godhead in one Person without confusion, change, division, or separation, the mystery of Tewahedo. Therefore we worship Him with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God in three Persons.

sections.quote: Glory be to the Holy Trinity, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, ONE GOD. Amen.
